title: Arrival of Sihyaj K'ahk' at Tikal, 378 CE
summary: According to epigrapher David Stuart's reading of Tikal Stela 31, the foreign warrior Sihyaj K'ahk' arrived at Tikal on 16 January 378 CE, the same day the text records the death of the king Jaguar Paw. Within about a year a new ruler, Yax Nuun Ahiin, took the throne, and Teotihuacan-style imagery appeared at the city.

uncertainty.note: The day is a correlation of the Long Count with the Christian calendar (Stuart gives 16 January 378 A.D.); other correlations or readings shift it by days. The year is not in dispute in the sources opened.

as_recorded.calendar: Maya Long Count and Calendar Round, with Christian date as given by Stuart

as_recorded.value: on January 16, 378 CE, the warrior Sihyaj K'ahk', possibly sent by Teotihuacan, conquered Tikal

where.historical_name: Tikal, Classic Maya city in the Petén lowlands (no modern state)

importance.justification: Marks the start of lasting Teotihuacan-linked political change at the leading Early Classic Maya kingdom.

sources.title: The Arrival of Strangers (Stuart, paper presented at Princeton, 1996)
sources.author: David Stuart

sources.title: Intraregional Relations in Pre-Columbian Mesoamerica: The Case of Tikal and Teotihuacan
sources.publisher: Portal magazine, LLILAS Benson, University of Texas at Austin

reviewer_note: Day-level date and the same-day-as-Jaguar-Paw-death reading depend on Stuart's interpretation, which his page calls debated. The Calendar Round month name (15 Mac) is as printed by Stuart and was not checked against a calendar table.
